name: light-speed

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows both colour bundles sweeping wide with the road curve clearly readable.

tagline: Streaks of pink and teal light rush down a dark highway.
summary: A night drive rendered in 3D: glowing car lights and lane markers stream toward the viewer and bend with the road. Holding the pointer speeds them up.
appearance: A black sky tops a dark road where dozens of neon streaks converge to a vanishing point. The left lanes glow magenta and purple, the right lanes teal and blue, and a white instruction line floats over the middle.
behaviour: The light trails stream toward the camera continuously, sweeping as the road bends. Pressing and holding the pointer accelerates the rush, then it eases back on release.
demo_content: The overlay line Click & hold to speed up.
use_when: A hero or splash wants a fast, atmospheric night-drive mood that reacts to a press.
avoid_when: A heavy 3D scene with bloom that needs a set height and a reasonably capable GPU.
customise: A single effectOptions object sets road width, lanes, length, field of view, speed-up and light counts; the shaders and layout are fixed.
weight_why: A Three.js highway with instanced lights and bloom rendered every frame.

a11y.note: Speed-up is hold-only and the WebGL scene has no label or keyboard path; reduced-motion is ignored.

issues: The road surface and lane markings are almost invisible; only the light streaks read.
The white instruction text competes with the brightest trails.
polish_why: Striking neon streaks and smooth motion; the road itself nearly disappears into black.
